segments.text: Design review. Sana has the onboarding screens and the accessibility review, Rahul has conflicts. Sana, start with the scary one.
Okay. So I went through Meridian's accessibility checklist with the tab bar on a five inch screen, which is what their field agents carry.
Rugged devices, and they wear gloves half the time.
The checklist says every primary navigation target has to be at least fifty-six dp, and navigation has to be a single landmark for the screen reader.
Our tab bar, with four tabs on a five inch screen, gives us about forty-eight dp per tab. That fails. I tried three tabs, still forty-eight because of the labels.
Can we drop the labels? Icons only?
Then it fails their no icon-only controls rule. I checked.
So the tab bar is dead?
The tab bar fails Meridian's checklist. My recommendation is a side drawer. Full width items, as tall as we want, one landmark, and it scales when we add sections later.
I mean... I'm not thrilled. Drawers hide things. Discoverability was the whole reason we picked the tab bar at kickoff.
I know. But this isn't our preference versus theirs, it's a hard requirement in their contract. Fifty-six dp or they don't sign off.
Also, honestly, their agents will use this app eight hours a day. They'll find the drawer.
Yeah. Yeah, okay. Fair.
Alright. Let's be explicit about this, because we are reversing a kickoff decision. At kickoff we chose a bottom tab bar, for discoverability.

We're reversing that. Decision: navigation is a side drawer. Rationale is Meridian's accessibility requirement, the fifty-six dp minimum touch target on five inch devices. That overrides discoverability.
Okay. Can I rip out the tab bar today?
Yes. When can the drawer be in?
The drawer's not hard. Side drawer implemented by Wednesday the 23rd.
The 23rd. And I'll send Meridian the drawer mockup for sign-off by Friday the 18th, so we don't get surprised twice.
I'll have the mockup to you tonight.
Now, I want to go further. If their checklist can kill the tab bar, it can kill anything. Sana, should it just be the baseline?
Yes. I was going to propose exactly that. Every screen gets checked against Meridian's accessibility checklist before we call it done.
Decision: Meridian's accessibility checklist is the baseline for every Orbit screen. Rationale, same as the drawer. It's contractual, and we'd rather find out in design than at sign-off.
Does that include the payment screens? Those are mostly Razorpay's SDK UI.
It includes anything we render. The SDK screens we can't change, I'll flag that to Meridian.
Okay. Onboarding screens, Sana.
Five screens, four done. Welcome, phone verification, PIN, permissions. The tour is the last one, three cards now.
And applying the same reasoning as the drawer: the primary buttons on onboarding go to fifty-six dp, full width. Right now they're forty-eight and centred.
Same precedent, same answer. Decision: onboarding buttons are fifty-six dp, full width. The drawer decision is the precedent.
That doesn't change my date. Onboarding screens still done by the 19th, with the new buttons.
Good. Rahul, conflicts.
Right. Conflict resolution for offline mode. I looked at three options: last-write-wins per record, last-write-wins per field, and manual merge.
Manual merge is the correct one and nobody will use it. Per record loses too much data. So I'm proposing last-write-wins per field, using the server timestamp.
Server timestamp, not device? Because device clocks on rugged Androids are a mess.
Server. The device sends its queue, the server stamps on arrival. Field-level means if I edit the meter reading and you edit the notes, we both win.
Any objections? Sana, from the UX side?
As long as the agent sees a this-record-was-updated toast, I'm fine.
Easy.
Decision: offline mode conflict resolution is last-write-wins per field, server timestamp. Rationale, it keeps the most data without asking agents to merge anything.
Priya, anything on payments?
Quick update. The UPI flow is still on for Friday the 25th. The polling workaround is in, and Razorpay's UPI intent flow works in sandbox now.
One risk. Meridian wants UPI autopay mandates for the subscription accounts, and Razorpay needs a merchant KYC step before mandates work in sandbox. I'm submitting that tomorrow.
How long does KYC take?
They say three business days. If it's more than that, I'll tell you by email, I won't wait for Monday.
Also, the offline payments question is still open. I'm building as if payments need connectivity. If that changes, tell me this week, not next.
Noted. I've asked Meridian twice. I'll escalate.
Hey, are we still on for the drawer sign-off on Friday? Because if Meridian bounces it I want to know before I build it.
Friday. I'll push them.
Okay, summary. Reversed: tab bar to side drawer, because of Meridian accessibility. New: the checklist is the baseline, fifty-six dp buttons, last-write-wins per field.
Dates: mockup sign-off the 18th, me. Onboarding the 19th, Sana. Drawer the 23rd, Rahul. UPI flow still the 25th, Priya.
That's right.
Good review. Thanks, all.
